answer: When autonomous agents bid on telemetry tasks like watching a canyon ledge for a falcon or scanning the horizon, concurrent memory-hard Proof-of-Work limits Sybil identities. At each epoch, every peer must submit an Argon2 solution bound to its public key and a live beacon within a short window. Because overlapping deadlines prevent time-sharing RAM across keys, an attacker pays dedicated memory capacity and bandwidth per alias, though wealthy cloud tenants can still rent parallel nodes.
